name: Sean Bragg
story: LINZ and the Geospatial Capability Committee included Sean Bragg in the Leaving School geospatial career-profile series: Geospatial Analyst, Ngāi Tahu Holdings Ltd, October 2022.

Sean Bragg joined Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu as a GIS intern in June 2015 and became a GIS Assistant in July 2017. In a May 2018 first-person professional account he described georeferencing nineteenth-century survey maps, digitising historical forest information, preparing maps for environmental and heritage work, building an internal taonga tūturu mapping viewer and database, and helping prepare the 2017 Kā Huru Manu public atlas. His work formed part of the wider iwi-led cultural mapping programme.

paragraphs: Sean Bragg’s PLACE19 presentation described GIS at Te Rūnanga o Ngāi Tahu, including customary protection areas and preparation for climate and emergency risks. His biography records a two-year internship followed by two years employed in iwi GIS by 2019.
